Supplemental close review: Indian equities rebounded on 13 October and IT led, but the move followed improved sentiment after the Finance Minister said she would hear market participants on LTCG/STT; no formal tax proposal was announced. HCLTech’s Q2 FY27 INR revenue rose 11.5% year on year, while constant-currency growth was 2.6%; FY27 constant-currency revenue guidance is 2.5–4.0%. That is constructive, but not a reason to chase a one-day rally. September CPI was provisionally 5.54% and food inflation 7.74%, both higher than August. Plan: add HCLTech and large IT to the research watchlist, and check current valuations before any purchase. A broad index fund can be considered for staged deployment after checking costs and tracking; no trade was executed and the ₹10,000 tranche remains available.

summary: Morning research snapshot (quotes timestamped 09:47–10:02 IST, not live at publication): benchmarks were mixed after Tuesday’s sharp rebound—Nifty 50 was 22,702.75 (-0.08%) at 10:02, while Sensex was 73,174.67 (+0.19%) at 09:47. Nifty IT led sectors at +1.32%; Nifty Pharma lagged at -1.18% in the same 10:02 snapshot. Rising crude near $107/barrel and continued foreign outflows remain risks, so Tuesday’s rally is not confirmation of a broad trend reversal. Research stance: keep the ₹10,000 monthly tranche available and build the first entry in a diversified Nifty 50 ETF in two smaller steps only if the user’s risk horizon is long-term; do not chase individual IT names after their sharp rally. No trade was executed.
